name: Omeprazole
summary: The original PPI — benchmark for the class; cheap, generic, and the reference point everything else is compared against.
good: First-line, cost-sensitive prescribing; well-established long-term safety data.
bad: Patients on clopidogrel where a lower-interaction PPI is preferred, or those who can’t reliably time doses before meals.
clinicalPearls: Because activation needs meal-stimulated acid secretion, taking it with or after food — a very common patient error — is one of the most frequent reasons for "PPI failure."
mechanism: Irreversible covalent inhibition of the parietal cell H⁺/K⁺-ATPase (proton pump) after acid-catalyzed activation to a reactive sulfenamide.
pharmacodynamics: Raises intragastric pH >4 for roughly 12–14h/day at steady state; nocturnal acid breakthrough is common.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Partial effect within hours, but full acid suppression needs 3–5 days as new pumps are progressively inhibited across doses.
pharmacokinetics.duration: ~24h from a single dose despite a short plasma half-life (~1h) — because inhibition is irreversible, duration tracks pump turnover, not drug clearance.
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic, mainly CYP2C19 with a CYP3A4 minor pathway. CYP2C19 poor metabolizers get higher exposure and stronger suppression; extensive/rapid metabolizers may be under-treated at standard doses.

indications: GERD, peptic ulcer disease, H. pylori eradication (triple therapy), NSAID gastroprotection, Zollinger–Ellison syndrome.
interactionNotes: Inhibits CYP2C19 → reduces conversion of clopidogrel to its active metabolite (contested but label-cautioned); reduces absorption of drugs needing low gastric pH (ketoconazole, atazanavir, iron salts).
